title: After torturing victim over missing drugs, Saskatoon man played VLTs, stabbed a stranger
summary: Within hours of participating in a brutally violent homicide, Dillon Singler went out and played some VLTs at Market Mall in Saskatoon, where he randomly attacked and stabbed another man.

image.caption: Dillon Singler has pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the February 2024 death of Lee Perkins in Saskatoon. (Saskatoon Court of King's Bench)

blocks.text: Warning: This story contains graphic descriptions of violence.
Within hours of participating in a brutally violent homicide, Dillon Singler went out and played some VLTs at Market Mall in Saskatoon, where he randomly attacked and stabbed another man.

Later on, his friend Edin Vrazalica messaged him to come back to the homicide scene in the Pacific Heights neighbourhood, to help clean up. Singler replied with the police news release about the stabbing at Market Mall, to show he had "heat" on him.
Vrazalica had a big job, cleaning the bloody scene where he and Singler had tortured Lee Perkins, questioning him about drugs that went missing on Feb. 1, 2024.
Perkins died when his throat was cut. The blood spatter reached up to the ceiling.

Both Singler and Vrazalica have pleaded guilty to manslaughter, and Vrazalica also pleaded guilty to offering an indignity to human remains. Earlier this month, Vrazalica was sentenced to 20 years in prison, and many details of the homicide were shared in court.

items: Judge imposes 20-year sentence in Saskatoon homicide

blocks.text: When Singler entered his plea last year, the details were under a publication ban to protect the fairness of upcoming trials. That ban was lifted after the last related jury trial concluded earlier this year.

Singler's sentencing hasn't happened yet, because the Crown embarked on a dangerous offender application. But when he pleaded, Singler signed a six-page agreed statement of facts with his "admissions."
According to those agreed facts, which were also signed by the Crown, Perkins was still alive when Singler left the torture scene.

What was Singler's role?
Perkins died at 610 Lisgar Avenue, the home of Vrazalica's then-girlfriend, Chantal McLaren.
Police tape surrounded the house where police found the body of Lee Perkins. (Liam O'Connor/CBC)

Perkins, 25, had travelled with Vrazalica and McLaren to transport a shipment of drugs from Vancouver to Saskatoon, arriving on Jan. 31, 2024. Vrazalica was a drug dealer, and had drawn Perkins into that world after they became friends at a construction job in Alberta a couple of years earlier.
Singler partied with them that night, into the early hours of Feb. 1.

Police found a video on Singler's phone of him and Vrazalica handling the new drugs, with text overlaid on the video saying "New Day Let's Get It." The drug was a liquid form of bromazolam, a benzodiazepine.

A screenshot from a video that showed men in masks dumping a pile of bottles onto a bed. The bottles were labeled as containing 'Codiene,' which was misspelled, but they actually contained bromazolam, a benzodiazepine. (Saskatoon Court of King's Bench)

Sometime after the party ended, someone called 911 reporting violence at the home. When patrol officers arrived at 10:22 a.m. on Feb. 1, Perkins was the only one there. He was sleeping, "noticeably intoxicated," on a couch upstairs.
Downstairs, officers found the drugs and seized them. They did not arrest or charge Perkins.

items: Police seized drugs from home, returned 2 days later to murder scene

blocks.text: When Vrazalica returned and found the drugs were gone, he "became enraged" and blamed Perkins.
"Vrazalica wanted Singler to assist him in getting information about the whereabouts of the drugs from Perkins and to punish Perkins for the drugs being missing," the agreed facts said.
"He also told Singler that he thought Perkins was giving drugs to McLaren and he was angry at the thought that she was going to relapse into addiction."
Lee Perkins's family members have been wearing purple shirts memorializing him, when they come to court. On the back, the shirts say, 'Justice for Lee.' (Hannah Spray/CBC)

The two men assaulted Perkins. According to the agreed facts, Singler cut off one of Perkins's fingers, and then recorded videos of Vrazalica cutting off other fingers. During one of them, McLaren could be heard crying in the background.
The last video was recorded at 8:18 p.m. on Feb. 1. Singler left at some point after that.
Stabbing at Market Mall
Later that night, in the very early hours of Feb. 2, Singler was at the Coachman Restaurant and Bar at Market Mall, playing the VLTs with another man, Dylan Wolfe.

At about 2:50 a.m., in the parking lot outside, Singler and Wolfe randomly attacked a stranger. Details about that attack came out in a trial held last year in Saskatoon provincial court for Singler and Wolfe, who were both charged with aggravated assault.
The stabbing victim testified that he and two friends had also played VLTs at the Coachman that night, and then sat talking in a car outside.

Two men they didn't know pulled up beside them in another vehicle. The victim rolled down his window and nodded as though to say, "What's up," then the two men got out of their vehicle and attacked him, and he ended up outside on the ground.
In the ensuing melee, the victim suffered three stab wounds to his back, one to his hip area, and another to his right lower torso. He didn't realize he had been stabbed until his friends told him.
Saskatoon police sent out a news release on Feb. 2, 2024, after a stabbing at Market Mall. (Saskatoon Police Service)
The victim's friends helped pull him away, and the two assailants drove off.
Surveillance video helped police identify the assailants. The video was also clear enough that Judge Jane Wootten said she could see it was Singler who stabbed the victim.
She convicted Singler of aggravated assault and Wolfe on the lesser charge of assault.
Singler's sentencing on the aggravated assault hasn't happened yet. It's been folded into the same dangerous offender application as the manslaughter conviction in the death of Lee Perkins.
'I need you bad or we are both done'
According to the agreed facts on Singler's guilty plea to manslaughter, Perkins was alive when Singler left 610 Lisgar Avenue, and the only other people there were Vrazalica and McLaren.
But sometime after Singler left on the evening of Feb. 1, Perkins was killed. On the morning of Feb. 2, McLaren went out and bought cleaning supplies.

A composite image shows, from left, Dillon Singler, Edin Vrazalica and Chantal McLaren, the three people who have pleaded guilty to charges in relation to the death of Lee Perkins. Singler and Vrazalica pleaded guilty to manslaughter, and McLaren pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact. (Saskatoon Court of King's Bench)
McLaren has pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact to murder.

The agreed facts filed at her sentencing earlier this year said she suffered "escalating and repeated physical, emotional and coercive abuse" at the hands of Vrazalica, and McLaren told the judge she was terrified for her safety and had begged for her life.

items: Woman bought cleaning supplies for murder scene 'at her abuser's direction'

blocks.text: On the afternoon of Feb. 2, Vrazalica messaged Singler, asking him to come back to the house: "I need you bad or we are both done iam busting my ass."
That's when Singler replied that he had heat on him, from the stabbing at Market Mall.

In the evening, Singler messaged Vrazalica: "Bro I just drove back to the city and don't even wanna come near that place fam, like yo I got you always but like this was your kid you brought down here and this was all cuz of your girl fam, like I'll pull up but I don't even see why I really need to but call back."
By that time, police were investigating the assault on Perkins, after receiving confidential information.

On the night of Feb. 2, officers set up surveillance outside 610 Lisgar Avenue while they prepared to get a warrant to go inside. Then, in the early hours of Feb. 3, they arrested McLaren after she left the home. Vrazalica came running outside with what appeared to be a weapon, and police shot him.
When police went inside, they found Perkins's remains, including his four severed fingers, stuffed inside a large plastic tote.
